I have been working this 2 mu for 45 years now, so I know this soil well. With well irrigation and only 2 mu, I cannot afford a bad season — even a small loss hurts when you only have two mu. My son lives in town now, so it is just me and my wife working the field.

For spring maize here in Quzhou, I sow around late April after the soil warms. I always buy a good hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or something similar that the dealer in town recommends. The old varieties yield maybe 400 kg per mu, but a good hybrid gives me 600 or more. The extra 30 yuan per mu on seed pays back many times.

For fertilizer, I do it the way that has worked for me. I apply diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer before sowing — about one bag (50 kg) covers my 2 mu, that gives me roughly 9 kg N and 11 kg P2O5 per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage (around late June), I top-dress with urea, about 20 kg per mu, which adds another 9 kg of N. Total nitrogen around 18 kg per mu — I used to apply more, but I learned that too much just makes the stalks fall over in summer storms. Potassium I add a little, maybe 5 kg per mu of potassium chloride, because our soil here is not too short of potash.

With well irrigation I can water when I need to. Spring maize needs water at sowing, then at jointing, tasseling, and grain filling — 4 times usually. If the summer rains come good in July, I skip one.

For pesticide: one spray for armyworm and corn borer around the whorl stage, one herbicide application after sowing, and sometimes a third if aphids get bad. Two to three applications.

I plough in autumn after harvest to bury stubble, then rotary till in spring before sowing. That has always been my way.
